# Chart Studio

> Create editable charts from URL-encoded JSON and embed them on any page with an iframe.

## Canonical URLs

- Documentation: https://tw-research.github.io/chart-studio/llms.txt
- Editor: https://tw-research.github.io/chart-studio/index.html

Chart Studio is a static GitHub Pages site. It needs no API key, account, build step, or server.

## Create a chart URL

Put a JSON chart specification in the `chart` query parameter. Use `URLSearchParams` so JSON is encoded safely:

```js
const chart = {
  type: "bar",
  title: "Sales by quarter",
  series: ["2025", "2026"],
  rows: [
    { label: "Q1", values: [12, 18] },
    { label: "Q2", values: [16, 24] },
    { label: "Q3", values: [21, 27] }
  ]
};

const url = new URL("https://tw-research.github.io/chart-studio/index.html");
url.searchParams.set("chart", JSON.stringify(chart));
console.log(url.href);
```

Opening that URL loads the chart into the editable Chart Studio interface.

## Embed a chart

Add `embed=1` to hide the editor and show only the responsive chart preview:

```js
url.searchParams.set("embed", "1");
```

Then embed the URL:

```html
<iframe
  src="https://tw-research.github.io/chart-studio/index.html?embed=1&chart=..."
  title="Sales by quarter"
  loading="lazy"
  style="width:100%;height:420px;border:0;"
></iframe>
```

This is the recommended way to display a generated chart from GitHub Pages. The chart is rendered in the viewer's browser.

## Download an image

Add `format=svg` or `format=png` to the chart URL. The browser renders the chart and starts a download:

```js
url.searchParams.set("format", "svg"); // downloads chart.svg
url.searchParams.set("format", "png"); // downloads chart.png
```

These are browser actions, not image API endpoints. They cannot be used directly as `<img src>` URLs or fetched by `curl`. Use `embed=1` for an iframe.

## Chart specification

Required:

- `type`: `likert`, `bar`, `stacked`, `column`, `stacked-column`, `line`, `area`, `scatter`, `donut`, or `pie`.
- `series`: an array of 1–50 string names.
- `rows`: an array of 1–500 objects. Each row has a string `label` and a numeric `values` array matching `series`.

Optional: `title`, `subtitle`, `lowLabel`, `highLabel`, `showCounts`, and `showGrid`. A supplied title or subtitle is displayed automatically. For Likert charts, values must be nonnegative integers, there can be at most 21 response points, and a row may use `group: "bipolar"` (default: `"agreement"`).

Example minimal specification:

```json
{"type":"pie","series":["Value"],"rows":[{"label":"Red","values":[4]},{"label":"Blue","values":[7]}]}
```

Chart data lives in the URL. Keep URLs reasonably short and do not put confidential information in shared links or browser history.
